prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key commitments and policies (2019 manifesto)

- Brexit and trade: Pass the existing deal, leave the EU in January; outside the single market, customs union, and ECJ; negotiate an EU free trade agreement by December 2020 with no extension; create up to 10 freeports; aim for 80% of UK trade covered by FTAs within three years (including USA, Australia, New Zealand, Japan); protect environmental, food and animal welfare standards; NHS not part of trade talks.

- Economy and tax: No rises in the rates of income tax, VAT or National Insurance; raise the National Insurance threshold to £9,500 (with an ambition for £12,500 tax-free income); increase the National Living Wage to two-thirds of median earnings by 2024 for over-21s; invest in infrastructure under fiscal rules (public investment averaging ≤3% of GDP); review and cut business rates for high streets; tackle tax avoidance and introduce a Digital Services Tax; raise R&D tax credit to 13%; review Entrepreneurs’ Relief.

- NHS and social care: Record funding uplift; 50,000 more nurses, 6,000 more GPs and 6,000 more primary care professionals; 50 million extra GP appointments; 40 new hospitals over 10 years and 20 upgrades; Innovative Medicines Fund; mental health legislative reform; free parking for those in greatest need; NHS excluded from trade deals; cross-party plan for long-term social care with a guarantee no one must sell their home to pay; £1bn extra per year for social care; one week statutory leave for unpaid carers; double dementia research funding.

- Education and skills: £14bn extra for schools over three years; minimum per-pupil funding of £5,000 (secondary) and £4,000 (primary); teacher starting salary to £30,000; arts premium and PE investment; more SEND places and funding; £500m for youth services; £3bn National Skills Fund; 20 Institutes of Technology; upgrade FE estate (~£2bn).

- Policing and justice: 20,000 more police; greater use of stop and search; tougher sentencing (end automatic halfway release for serious crimes; whole-life terms for child murder); knife crime orders; 10,000 extra prison places; national cyber crime force and National Crime Laboratory; Victims’ Law and Domestic Abuse Bill; parole and criminal justice reviews.

- Immigration: Australian-style points-based system; bespoke routes (e.g., NHS visa, top talent); equal treatment of EU and non-EU; five-year residency before most benefits; increased NHS surcharge; EU citizens’ existing rights guaranteed.

- Housing: Support long-term fixed-rate mortgages to lower deposits; discounted homes for local/key workers; reform shared ownership and leasehold (peppercorn ground rents; ban new leasehold houses); end no-fault evictions and introduce a lifetime deposit; target 300,000 homes a year by mid-2020s; £10bn Single Housing Infrastructure Fund; end rough sleeping by end of Parliament; stamp duty surcharge on non-resident buyers.

- Infrastructure and connectivity: Northern Powerhouse Rail (Leeds–Manchester) and Midlands Rail Hub; reform rail franchising; restore some Beeching lines; superbus networks and an all‑electric bus town; £1bn rapid EV charging network; consult on earliest phase‑out of new petrol/diesel cars; major pothole programme; cycling fund and standards; nationwide gigabit broadband by 2025 with £5bn for hard‑to‑reach areas.

- Environment and energy: Net Zero by 2050; Environment Bill and Office for Environmental Protection; £640m Nature for Climate Fund (75,000 acres of trees annually) and peatland restoration; plastics levy, extended producer responsibility, deposit return scheme, ban plastic waste exports to non‑OECD; £4bn for flood defences; offshore wind to 40GW by 2030; £800m for first carbon capture cluster by mid‑2020s; £500m to decarbonise industry; support hydrogen, nuclear and fusion; fracking moratorium; £9.2bn for energy efficiency in homes, schools and hospitals; clean air legislation.

- Work, welfare and families: Continue Universal Credit with improvements; end benefit freeze; reduce disability reassessments; National Strategy for Disabled People; protect pensioner benefits and triple lock; £1bn for wraparound childcare; flexible working consultation; neonatal leave; stronger protections after maternity.

- Rural, farming and fishing: Replace CAP with “public money for public goods” while maintaining farm budgets through the Parliament; expand seasonal workers scheme; leave the Common Fisheries Policy with legal sustainability duties; boost rural broadband/mobile; tackle rural crime.

- Democracy and constitution: Repeal Fixed-term Parliaments Act; equalise parliamentary boundaries; voter ID at polling stations; extend overseas voting rights; maintain voting age at 18; strengthen protections for free speech and the press; constitutional review (courts, Parliament, prerogative, judicial review, human rights).

- Security, defence and foreign policy: Exceed 2% of GDP on defence and increase by at least 0.5% above inflation annually; modernise forces, maintain nuclear deterrent, invest in cyber and establish Space Command; support veterans (NI break for employers, railcard, childcare, guaranteed interviews); Magnitsky-style sanctions; maintain 0.7% GNI on aid; champion girls’ education, media freedom, anti‑slavery; end preventable maternal and child deaths by 2030.

- Animal welfare: Tougher cruelty sentences; crack down on puppy smuggling; animal sentience law; end excessively long live-animal journeys; extend ivory ban; ban trophy imports; ban primates as pets; new measures to tackle cat theft.
